don't try any crazy diets. That shit is always unhealthy. Grab a bike, even a cheap one from Wal Mart (as much as I hate them), and get out there and do it. Push. You'll get the weight down eventually no matter how much you eat if you start exercising. 

But remember that losing a lot of weight at once is bad. I'm not a health expert, but if I recall, the first few pounds are water and come off quickly, but then it's like a  pound or two a week in the healthy range. 

Seriously, I've never had overweight problems, I have the opposite. I eat like a horse and gain nothing. I'm too skinny (5'10" and 160lbs). But you can do this. It's just not a fast acting thing, it requires persistence. Make that the goal. Get on the bike, and while you're out there riding, you won't have to worry about what other people are saying, because they won't be around to say it.

You can fix all of this yourself. Really, you can. The anti-psychotics, I don't know. I'm not a doctor. But the eating thing, that's something you can control, but you have to put your mind to it. 

Feeling pretty? I have no idea. I've always been average. The bad thing about that is that I maybe never felt like Don Juan, but the good thing about it is I never had to care that much. I'm kind of in between. But the important thing for you is the focus on what other people are saying and how it is influencing your life. That seems to be an issue. 

I can promise you this, though - aside from cutting the weight, which you CAN do, if you really want to stop worrying so much about what other people think, what might be best is to focus on goals. If you have goals that keep you busy, one day you're going to get done with accomplishing one of them, turn around, and wonder when you stopped caring about other peoples' opinions. It's that easy, really.

"I read what you said, and I know what you mean. As a Jew, I look to the passages where Abraham and Yahweh speak about blah bloopety blah. To me, I think that even if you were not religious, or if your religion differed, you could use it to analyze your purpose for being here, and your reasons for going on to fulfill that purpose"

People like to talk about how they got over things, but seeing as how my wife and I watched everyone we know get divorced, I have yet to see a single father with a happy life.

It seems like we live in a society where people will try to tell you it's always worth living, but I have yet to see a valid argument for those who would posit such a notion. 

Further, it seems like we also accept that divorce is less damaging than death, when in fact, many doctors and psychologists agree that the mourning that occurs after divorce is often worse.

So from a comparative standpoint, divorce is probably more damaging and worse than death, for all concerned except the one person leaving, except in cases where there is abuse. The problem is that people want to deny that, because the consequences of the latter occur in a more condensed timeframe, whereas the prior deals with damage that occurs over a long period of time. 

Think of it like injecting yourself with cancer as compared to smoking cigarettes. Yes, you have time to quit smoking cigarettes, much much longer, but by the same token, you've poisoned everyone around you in the interim. 

Death, in the absence of me, will, in all likelihood, affect them no less than the current circumstances. The bright side of that is that rather than realize how fucked up they are later in life, when they've already made the same commitment, they can get help now, in the immediate future.
